correctness.rationale: For every fixed r, Dirichlet beta-sum integration gives the exact factorial moment (q)_r ((q-r)a)^(up m)/(qa)^(up m). A uniform logarithmic product expansion has error O_r((a+1)/q), tending to zero when a~kappa log q, and the prescribed centering gives factorial moments e^(-rx). This proves a Poisson vacancy limit and hence a Gumbel cover time. The posterior Beta(a,(q-1)a+m) law for an unseen label has normalized mean tending to e^(-1/kappa) and variance tending to zero. Tightness of vacancy counts and a lower cutoff in the Gumbel window prove the final-label mark. Boundary conditions q->infinity, fixed kappa>0, real x and positive a are explicit. Rational verifier checks finite identities; infinite claims follow analytically.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A statement of fixed-concentration Fréchet convergence cannot imply a Gumbel limit under concentrations diverging like log q; the assumptions are disjoint. Classical deterministic-weight coverage theorems might support the time marginal after conditional random-environment analysis, but the explicit annealed factorial-moment limit and terminal label posterior concentration are separate steps. Other close published records concern fixed masses, a different reinforcement mechanism, covariance crossings or deterministic Zipf weights. This is best-knowledge originality, not an independence claim.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is equivalently an annealed Gumbel limit for occupancy-vacancy factorial moments in the symmetric Dirichlet–multinomial sample at shape a_q~kappa log q, with a joint terminal-latent-weight statement. Holst proves a Fréchet limit when the latent iid gamma weight law is fixed as q grows. His fixed-shape assumptions do not cover a_q increasing logarithmically. The finite reinforced-urn coverage tail and covariance results do not imply the moving-shape Gumbel normalization or final latent weight. No matching formulation was identified in the checked sources; searching alone cannot establish global novelty.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Holst (fixed shape) and Neal (deterministic unequal rates), plus published records of reinforced-urn cover time, Dirichlet-multinomial covariances, Pólya–Friedman dynamics and marked Zipf coupons, did not identify the same moving-shape annealed completion and terminal-mass joint result. Holst is credited for the fixed-shape Fréchet law and random-rate embedding. Broader triangular-array extreme-value literature and uninspected records remain priority risks.
residual_risks: A very general moving-distribution extreme-value theorem could cover the annealed Gumbel marginal indirectly.
Some close public abstracts had no accessible full text, so their appendices and implicit corollaries were not conclusively checked.
Priority, especially of the terminal latent-mass concentration at the logarithmic shape scale, requires independent domain-expert assessment.

value.rationale: Symmetric Pólya sampling with a growing number of colors provides a natural interpolation between heterogeneous fixed-Dirichlet reinforced coverage and ordinary uniform coupon collection. Logarithmic per-color mass is a motivated critical regime where color weights concentrate while rare terminal colors retain a nontrivial systematic bias. Exact centering, Gumbel crossover and the final coupon’s latent rarity quantify this transition and are not merely generic finite algebra, renaming or a marginal limit already displayed in the closest literature.
